territorial_scope.description: Applies to online activity conducted in or from Singapore or perceived by persons in Singapore; Part 5 directions, orders and information notices may be given to individuals and entities whether inside or outside Singapore, and offences committed abroad may be dealt with as if committed in Singapore.

summary.short: Creates offences and civil torts for twelve online harmful activities, including harassment, doxxing, intimate image abuse and inauthentic (possibly AI-generated) material. Sets up a Commissioner of Online Safety with power to issue directions and orders to individuals, administrators and online services, plus reconsideration and appeal. Commencement is set by Ministerial notification.
summary.long: The Act defines twelve online harmful activities (Part 3), including online harassment, doxxing, intimate image abuse, image-based child abuse, online impersonation and inauthentic material abuse, which covers audio, visual or audiovisual material altered or generated by digital means such as generative AI. Eligible victims may report to a Commissioner of Online Safety (Part 4). The Commissioner may give Part 5 directions to communicators, administrators and online service providers, such as stop-communication, access-disabling, right-of-reply, labelling and account-restriction directions, and may issue orders following non-compliance, including access blocking orders to internet access providers and app removal orders. Part 6 gives information-gathering powers and allows end-user identity collection notices to prescribed online service providers. Part 7 provides reconsideration and appeal to an Online Safety Appeal Panel. Part 8 creates offences for non-compliance and for false information. Parts 10 to 12 create civil torts and administrator and online service provider duties to respond to online harm notices. Part 13 governs damages and remedies, and Part 15 amends the Defamation Act 1957, the Protection from Harassment Act 2014, the Family Justice Act 2014 and the Info-communications Media Development Authority Act 2016.

notes: The document is the Bill as first read (Bill No. 18/2025), not an enacted text. Commencement is by ministerial notification and may be staggered (s 1(1)-(2)); registry metadata lists status partially_in_force. The Schedule referred to in s 109 is headed at the end but its text is not in the document. target_instrument_id is empty because no registry IDs for the cited Acts were provided. Wording differs between s 19 (Part 3 definition: would increase the risk of harm; the Commissioner may consider) and s 87 (Part 10 tort: would cause harm; the court may have regard). Parts 3 and 10 to 12 apply only to activities whose Part 3 definitions have been brought into operation. This part covers the Schedule (operative POHA amendments, paragraphs 1 to 25) and the explanatory statement, clause summaries and expenditure note. Operative text of clauses 1 to 111 outside the Schedule is not reproduced here, so the amendments to the Defamation Act 1957, PSIA 2007, Family Justice Act 2014 and IMDA Act 2016 are recorded from clause summaries only. Target IDs are null because no registry IDs were given. Possible inconsistency: the explanatory note on Schedule paragraph 10(c) says an administrator may apply to vary, suspend or cancel an expedited protection order under section 13(3A)(c), but the amending words in paragraph 10(d) only insert a reference to an administrator ordered to stop publication.
